title: Quant profile traceability and reproducibility playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: define and implement a deterministic, auditable flow for producing quantization artifacts (FP8/INT8 profiles and calibration outputs) so any artifact in storage can be traced back to a reproducible build recipe and safely swapped out in production. Problem: calibration runs today depend on transient state (CUDA/cuDNN versions, nondeterministic random seeds, dataloader ordering, mixed-precision kernels) and artifacts are stored without a standardized trace record. That makes debugging accuracy regressions slow and risky for roll-forwards or rollbacks. This ticket captures the playbook: reproducible build runner, canonical recipe schema, content signatures, signed metadata, storage aliasing, and an automated accuracy gate for candidate artifacts.
proposed_solution: 1) Define a small, strict calibration recipe schema (model version, quant profile, dataset snapshot id, seed, batch sizes, runtime flags, torch/cuda/driver pins). 2) Implement a hermetic build runner (containerized orchestration) that records the full environment and emits a deterministic artifact and a content signature (SHA256 over canonicalized bytes + recipe). 3) Store artifacts in object storage under content-addressed keys and maintain an alias layer (eg. latest-approved/production) to enable atomic swaps. 4) Attach a signed audit record (builder identity + CI run ID + eval metrics) for each candidate. 5) Add an automated accuracy validation harness that runs the artifact against a locked eval set and enforces metric deltas before allowing alias promotion. 6) Provide tooling for safe revert: alias switch + post-rollback validation + incident note template.
acceptance_criteria: Given a calibration recipe and seed, re-running the hermetic runner produces an artifact whose content signature matches the stored signature
Every artifact stored has an attached signed audit record linking to CI run, recipe, and environment snapshot
Promotion to production alias is blocked unless the automated accuracy harness reports metrics within configured thresholds
A rollback can be executed via alias swap within the Console and is reflected in the audit log with a signed entry
Engineering runbook exists with CLI commands for reproduce -> validate -> promote -> revert
milestones: Schema: finalize calibration recipe schema and canonicalization rules (PR to docs)
Runner: implement hermetic build runner with explicit seed control and environment capture
Signature: compute deterministic content signature and sign metadata with CI key
Storage: implement content-addressed layout + aliasing API and Console UI hooks
Validate: build and integrate accuracy validation harness with gating in CI
Docs & Runbook: publish step-by-step playbook and incident template
risks: Full determinism may be infeasible on certain GPU kernels — mitigation: record nondeterministic ops and force a checksum-based validation rather than bitwise equality
Long-running calibration jobs increase CI cost — mitigation: sample-based quick checks for PR validation and full harness for candidate promotion
Secrets/key management for artifact signing adds ops burden — mitigation: use existing KMS integration and short-lived signing tokens
Alias swaps might cause cache incoherence in serving layer — mitigation: small rollout windows and automatic prefix cache invalidation
notes: Related work: ENG-17643 (calibration fingerprint), ENG-21002 (calibration replay indexing)
Proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5421 - adds recipe schema and canonicalizer
S3 staging path for artifacts: s3://redwood-quant-artifacts/staging/
implementation_steps: Draft recipe schema and canonicalization rules in RFC
Add containerized hermetic runner to CI with pinned base images
Implement signature generator that concatenates sorted JSON recipe + artifact bytes and computes SHA256
Wire artifact storage buckets for content-addressed storage and alias records
Extend Console APIs to show artifact provenance and allow alias promotions/reverts
Add CI gate that runs validation harness and requires green before promotion
testing_plan: Unit tests for canonicalizer and signature generator (determinism across machines)
Integration test: run runner twice in different CI agents -> verify signature equality
End-to-end: promote candidate to staging alias, run canary serving test, measure latency and accuracy delta
Failure test: simulate a bad candidate and verify alias-based revert restores expected metrics
